sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking following reliefs:-
"10.1 That, the Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondent authorities to call the entire records pertaining to this case.
10.2

That, this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to issue writ in the nature of certiorari,
prohibition and mandamus, directing the respondent authorities to decide pending representation (Annexure P/3) pertaining to claim of just and fair compensation in lieu of by modifying the existing measurement/assessment report/award, and further to prohibit the authorities from asking the petitioner to vacate her land and house forcefully without providing her modified just and fair compensation, and further to pass any other order which deems fit including cost of the petition in the interest of justice.
2.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was owner of the land bearing Khasra No. 264/5 and 265/6 admeasuring total 0.016 hectares.
She was in possession of the said land by constructing house and also the boundary wall.
The land of the petitioner was acquired by the Respondent No. 4/Sub-Divisional Officer for the Respondent No. 1.

However, the compensation Pun Bai vs South Eastern Coalfield Limited on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138493378/
1 is determined/computed without proper measurement of the area of the land as also, the construction and therefore, the petitioner submitted representations (Annexure P/3) before the Respondent No. 1

However, the representation of the petitioner is not decided.

3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Respondents No. 1 & 2 would submit that the land of the petitioner was acquired under the provisions of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition &
Development) Act, 1957 (hereinafter for brevity referred to as the Act, 1957).
He however, submits that they will consider and decide the representations (Annexure P/3) as submitted by the petitioner.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the documents placed on record along with the writ petition.

5. Perusal of the pleadings made in the writ petition as also the documents would show that the grievance of the petitioner is with respect to the determining the compensation, without measuring the area of the land or the construction meaning thereby, at the time of acquisition of the property of the petitioner under the Act, 1957, the amount of compensation is determined.

Under the Act, 1957 the petitioner is having the efficacious remedy of approaching the Tribunal constituted by the respondents for determining the compensation, if the petitioner is aggrieved with the computation of the amount of compensation by the Central Government.
Section 14 of the Act, 1957 deals with method of determining compensation.
Sub-section 1 of Section 14 of the Act, 1957 provides that where the amount of any compensation payable under this Act can be fixed by agreement, it shall be paid in accordance with such agreement.

Sub-section 2 of Section 14 of the Act, 1957 provides that where no such agreement can be reached, the Central Government shall constitute the Tribunal consisting of a person who is or has been or is qualified to be a Judge of a High Court for the purpose of determining the amount.
The District Judge, Bilaspur is authorized to act as a Tribunal under the Act, 1957 with respect to the territory in which the land of the petitioner comes.

6. As the grievance of the petitioner is with respect to computation of the amount of compensation,
the petitioner is having the efficacious remedy to approach the Tribunal for determination of the amount of compensation and further, the appeal is also provided against the order of determination of the amount of compensation by the Tribunal.
7.
In the aforementioned facts of the case, where the petitioner is having the efficacious alternate remedy under the Act, 1957, I am not inclined to entertain this writ petition.
Accordingly, this writ petition is dismissed reserving liberty with the petitioner to avail the efficacious remedy available to him under the Act, 1957.
8. With the aforesaid observation, this writ petition is dismissed.
